texts.preamble: Irfan vs State Of U.P. on 22 November, 2023 Author: Samit Gopal Bench: Samit Gopal High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad ?Neutral Citation No. - 2023:Ahc:221771 Court No. - 69 Case :- Criminal Revision No. - 2628 of 2013 Revisionist :- Irfan Opposite Party :- State of U.P. Counsel for Revisionist :- Sushil Kumar Pandey Counsel for Opposite Party :- Govt. Advocate Hon'ble Samit Gopal,J. 1. List revised.
texts.arguments: 6. At the outset, learned counsel for the revisionist does not challenge his conviction, but submits that he is ready and willing to apply for commutation of sentence on the condition of further deposit, if any, in lieu of awarded sentence. Learned counsel for the revisionist submits that the revisionist is aged about 68 years as of now as his date of birth is 01.08.1956 as per Aadhar Card. 7. Learned A.G.A. submits that the sentence is proportionate to the charge established. He also submits that no useful purpose would be served by keeping this revision pending and it be disposed of by giving appropriate directions. 8. It is not disputed that the alleged offence took place on 23.04.1999, when the alleged sample of cream was purchased from the revisionist. Learned A.G.A. is right in his submission that this Court cannot tinker, where minimum sentence is provided under a statute like the P.F.A. Act, 1954. 9. The Apex Court in the case of State of Rajasthan Vs. Jagdish Prasad : (2009) 12 SCC 646 held in paras-4 and 5 thereof as under: "4. In Dayal Singh v. State of Rajasthan it was inter alia observed as follows: (SCC pp. 728-29, para 15) "15. In the instant case it was not disputed that for the offence charged a minimum sentence of 6 months' rigorous imprisonment is prescribed by law. The appellant has been sentenced to undergo 6 months' rigorous imprisonment which is the minimum sentence.
